testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Joggers wearing headsets:

options.text: Usually notice what is happening around them.
May not notice what is happening around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not notice what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear traffic sounds clearly and may not know you are there.

questions.question: Hanging meat cargo:

options.text: Is stable because of how it is loaded.
Can cause problems because animals may be attracted to the smell.
Is unstable because it has a high center of gravity.
Should not be transported in summer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is unstable because it has a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Drive carefully when transporting hanging meat. This load is unstable because it has a high center of gravity and the meat swinging can affect your control of the vehicle.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes on the road ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Block in the driver with your vehicle.
Stop safely near the crash and report the aggressive behavior to police.
Pull over and yell at the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely near the crash and report the aggressive behavior to police.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop a safe distance away. Wait for police and tell them about the aggressive behavior you saw.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sign of tire failure?
questions.explanation: Tire failure signs include a loud bang from a blowout or a heavy thumping feeling. If steering feels heavy or the rear slides, stop and check your tires.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose grip on the road.
The trailer comes loose from the tractor.
The vehicle becomes easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, tires can lose grip and slide on water. This is called hydroplaning. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts must be all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Check that all lug nuts are present, free of cracks and damage, and tight. Look for rust trails or shiny threads that show looseness. Check bolt holes for cracks and damage.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must complete all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass the HazMat knowledge test, complete a security threat check, prove U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, and get an FBI fingerprint check and criminal background check.

questions.question: If a trailer has Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS) but the tractor does not:

options.text: The truck cannot be driven because both must have ABS.
Get a new tractor with ABS.
The tractor and trailer can still be used together.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor and trailer can still be used together.
questions.explanation: Having anti-lock brakes on just the tractor or just the trailer gives you better control when braking.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You don't need to use a turn signal.

questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly to keep control. This gives other drivers time to move if you didn't see them. Always use your turn signal.

questions.question: Frequent blinking may be a sign of fatigue.
questions.explanation: Frequent blinking, trouble focusing, and heavy eyelids are signs of fatigue. If you are tired, stop driving and get off the road.

questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Should take over-the-counter medicine to stay awake.
May make important decisions too slowly.
Is usually more careful than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May make important decisions too slowly.
questions.explanation: When you are tired, you will not see or react to dangers as quickly as when you are awake and alert. Your ability to make important decisions will be weaker.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system is letting out air:

options.text: You should not worry. This is normal.
Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve in an air brake system releases air to stop the pressure from getting too high. If the valve starts releasing air, something is wrong. Have a mechanic repair it.

questions.question: What happens if you fail the air brakes test?

options.text: You cannot drive vehicles with air brakes.
Your CDL will have an air brake endorsement marked with an asterisk.
Your CDL will not be valid.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot drive vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: If you do not take or pass the air brakes test, you will only be allowed to drive vehicles without air brakes.

questions.question: When you start an engine, the oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.explanation: Check your truck's gauges when starting the engine. Oil pressure should reach normal level within a few seconds after the engine starts.

questions.question: When carrying cargo, you should inspect it:

options.text: Only after the trip is over.
Every time you stop for a break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you stop for a break.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo and how it is fastened every time you take a break during a trip. Inspect it at least every 150 miles.

questions.question: If a vehicle is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: If someone is following too closely, create more space in front of your vehicle to make it easier for them to pass. Driving faster is a bad idea because they may keep tailgating at the higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, keep ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length.
questions.explanation: At speeds under 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. At faster speeds, add at least one more second.

questions.question: When driving in heavy traffic, you should:

options.text: Use your cell phone for texts instead of calls.
Turn up the volume on your cell phone.

questions.explanation: Heavy traffic, road work, many pedestrians, or bad weather all need your full attention. Avoid all distractions, including cell phone use, in these areas.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:
questions.explanation: Always follow posted speed limits in work zones. Slow down if road or weather conditions are bad. Slow down even more if workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: When changing lanes, your turn signal:

options.text: Should only be used when other traffic is present.
Should only be used from dusk until dawn.

questions.explanation: Always signal properly before turning or changing lanes.

questions.question: If wheel bearing seals are leaking, what should you do?

options.text: Add more grease until the seal is full.
Add brake fluid to the bearing.

questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check that wheel bearing seals are not leaking. If you find anything unsafe, have it fixed. Laws require that you do not drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: How should you park to make it safest to leave a stop?

options.text: So you must back up to leave your space.
So you can pull forward to leave your space.
On the side of a road, not in a parking lot.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can pull forward to leave your space.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous. When possible, park so you can pull forward to leave your space instead of backing up.

questions.question: How much water on a road surface causes hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when a vehicle's tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. Only a small amount of water is needed for this to happen.

questions.question: What happens if you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: You automatically fail the basic vehicle control skills test.
You get an extra point against your score.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, always face the vehicle and keep three points of contact. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a distracted driver on the road?
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, give them plenty of space. Be extra careful if you pass them because they may not see you and could drift into your lane.

questions.question: What lights should you use when visibility is poor and you are near other drivers?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when traveling near other drivers in poor visibility, such as at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather. High beams can make it hard for other drivers to see.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, what should be your main way to control speed?
questions.explanation: On steep downhills, use engine braking as your main speed control method. Downshift before going down the hill. Using brakes too much can cause them to overheat and stop working well.

questions.question: Is a rear tire with 1/32 inch tread depth acceptable?
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth in every groove. Other tires must have at least 2/32 inch of tread depth.

questions.question: What might you be asked to do during a vehicle inspection test for a CDL?
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you may be asked to check the engine oil level in the engine compartment.

questions.question: Is texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle allowed?

options.text: Yes, if the text is work-related.
Yes, if the message has fewer than 10 words.
Yes, because it is safer than talking on the phone.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle is illegal and dangerous. This includes typing or reading text on any electronic device.

questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: Protect the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or hard stop.
Protect the driver's head when entering the cab of a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or hard stop.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver from cargo that moves forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system poses no threat to the driver.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous. It can allow toxic fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: When are drivers usually the least alert?
questions.explanation: Drivers are usually less alert late at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: When a vehicle starts, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off within a few seconds.
Stay on until you manually turn them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and anti-lock brakes should turn off right away.

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air pressure can leak away over time, so emergency brakes in an air brake system must use mechanical force to stay engaged.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the vehicle running and in gear.
Check the lights from inside the vehicle.
Check the lights using a reflection from a shiny surface.

questions.explanation: To check your lights, set the parking brake, turn off the engine, and remove the key. Turn on your low beam headlights and four-way flashers. Get out of the vehicle to check that all lights are working.

questions.question: How often must you check that cargo is secure?

options.text: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving.
Only after traveling up a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safe and secure throughout the trip.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because the driver cannot see everything behind them. Avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a distracted driver on the road?
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, give them plenty of room and keep a safe following distance.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable?

options.text: Dual tires that do not touch each other
Mismatched tire sizes if used only on short trips
Retreaded tires on the front of a school bus

questions.correctAnswerText: Dual tires that do not touch each other
questions.explanation: Dual tires must not touch each other or other vehicle parts. Tire sizes must match. Retreaded, regrooved, or recapped tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus. Tires must not be cut or damaged.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT cause hydraulic brake failure?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure usually happens for two reasons: loss of hydraulic pressure or brake fade from overuse on long hills.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Only be used when it is wet outside.
Be used to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from the air tanks. Always drain the tank completely when using the drain.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle loses its ABS?

options.text: Push the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.explanation: ABS prevents brakes from locking up during hard braking. If ABS fails, your basic brakes still work. You can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.explanation: If confronted by an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact or gesture at them. Report them to authorities when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When making tight maneuvers, it is important for a driver to:

options.text: Open their door for a better look.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. Check them especially often when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops the compressor from pumping air once the air tanks reach:
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when air tanks reach 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: A vehicle must be equipped with all of the following, except:

options.text: Warning devices for a parked vehicle.

questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must carry emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, warning triangles or flares, and a charged fire extinguisher. A flashlight is not required.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best advice for driving in fog?

options.text: Try not to drive in fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try not to drive in fog.
questions.explanation: Avoid driving in fog if possible. If you must drive in fog, use low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: A sign indicating a maximum safe speed:

options.text: Is suggesting a driving speed, but vehicles may travel faster than the posted speed.
Is suggesting a speed limit to be followed only by vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds.
Should be followed and no vehicle should travel faster than the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be followed and no vehicle should travel faster than the posted speed.
questions.explanation: Never exceed the speed shown on a maximum safe speed sign.
